newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Malaysia's investment arm in high-tech investments.
newsitem.headline: Malaysia's investment arm in high-tech investments.

text.p: Khazanah Nasional Bhd, the Malaysian government's investment arm, has invested 790.62 million ringgit ($313.74 million) in six companies involved in strategic and high-technology industries.

The national Bernama news agency on Thursday quoted Deputy Prime Minister Anwar Ibrahim saying that the companies include MCIC Holdings Sdn Bhd (3 million ringgit with a 10 percent shareholding) and Putrajaya Holdings Sdn Bhd (61.2 million ringgit for a 40 percent share).

The other companies are Wafer Technology (M) Sdn Bhd (400,000 ringgit with a 40 percent share), Usahasama Proton-DRB (65 million ringgit with a 15 percent share) and Motosikal dan Enjin Nasional Bhd (15 million ringgit with a 15 percent share), Bernama reported.

The single largest investment by Khazanah is in satellite concern Measat Broadcasting Sdn Bhd at 646.02 million ringgit for a 15 percent shareholding, Anwar said in a written reply in Parliament on Thursday.
Khazanah was formed to hold and manage existing government investments and to make new investments in strategic and high-technology industries.
